text: What changed in 1956? Pakistan adopted its first constitution and formally transitioned into a republican parliamentary framework.
Did the 1956 constitution solve East Pakistan's representation crisis? It addressed structure but did not fully resolve disputes over parity, autonomy, and real power sharing.
Why does this event matter in Bengal history? It shows how constitutional design without political trust can institutionalize conflict instead of settling it.
A constitutional settlement without equitable representation remained politically fragile.
